text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 5.3% today after oil prices surged on escalating Iran-U.S. tensions—crude rose sharply following Treasury Secretary Bessent's announcement that all Iranian airlines will be shut down starting Wednesday. While refiners typically benefit when oil prices rise (they buy crude cheap and sell refined products), this particular oil spike is driven by geopolitical risk rather than demand strength, which can hurt refiner margins if crude rallies faster than gasoline and diesel prices follow.

The stock's sharp reversal is notable: it had climbed steadily for four straight days through last Thursday, then pulled back sharply over the weekend and today. The messaging from Washington has been mixed—Trump suggested openness to talks with Iran on Friday, which sent oil below $100, but the administration has since tightened its stance, unsettling markets and creating the kind of volatile, supply-shock-driven oil environment that refiners find difficult to navigate profitably.
